leaking_backend_assumptions.leaks_into: the SecretSpec manifest, not Blaine code
leaking_backend_assumptions.detail: Vault and OpenBao carry mount/path in the alias URI, while AWS demands a per-secret ref. A manifest carrying an AWS-shaped ref stopped resolving against the dotenv backend in this test, so ref is backend-coupling rather than neutral addressing.
leaking_backend_assumptions.evidence: OBSERVED: the same fixture resolved without ref and reported "required but not set" with ref

leaking_backend_assumptions.leaks_into: the alias definition and operator procedure
leaking_backend_assumptions.detail: BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN, VAULT_TOKEN, BAO_TOKEN and the AWS chain are different bootstraps. Blaine withholds all of them from consumers identically, but the rotation runbook names the one in use.
AWS needs a region; Vault and OpenBao need host, mount and optionally a namespace.
AWS and Vault expose versioned secrets. Nothing in this spike exercised version pinning, and Blaine does not model a version today.
Blaine only reads. secretspec set and delete differ across backends but are outside the materialization path used here.

verdict.portability_at_blaine_code_level: PROVED for substitution; no Blaine source byte changed across a live backend swap
verdict.portability_at_declaration_level: Vault and OpenBao expected to need only an alias change; AWS additionally needs a per-secret manifest ref unless names match
